reasons: Classification is correct: TrueLink's indemnity in p0073/p0075 covers only its own breach/non-performance, with no IP infringement prong anywhere in the agreement, so the clause fails even the fallback position (which requires a Vendor IP indemnity). This is a genuine deviation, not an acceptable fallback.

The redline is valid and directionally right: it preserves the original breach/non-performance prong and appends IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct prongs to the existing vendor indemnity — the smallest edit that reaches the playbook position, and it uses terms present in the document (Interface, Client Content) with a catch-all for deliverables.

The failed regex check ('vendor indemnity for IP infringement present') is a phrasing artifact — the inserted text expressly covers allegations that the Interface/Services 'infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property right'. The 0.756 changed-character ratio is expected when adding four new indemnity prongs to a single short clause and does not indicate over-editing.
Comment is accurate, concise, on-tone, cites the playbook position, and offers the customary exclusions/remedies fallback as a trade.

Noted but not fatal: the drafter did not narrow Client's broad indemnity in p0071–p0072 and did not add an express 'defend' obligation or a 3x super-cap. The fallback position does not condition compliance on narrowing the Customer indemnity, and these are sub-elements short of preferred wording appropriately handled in the rationale rather than blocking the fix to the core deficiency.
